claims.text: The starting material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Adding a small amount of Y to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance.
Adding a small amount of Ce to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance.
Y or Ce addition will produce a protective oxide layer on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The reactive-element-containing oxide layer will be stable and adherent.
The stable, adherent oxide layer will prevent further oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Reactive-element addition will reduce oxidation relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Reactive-element addition will reduce pesting relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Reactive-element addition will preserve the alloy's useful high-temperature tensile ductility.
Reactive-element addition will preserve the alloy's useful high-temperature yield strength.
Reactive-element addition will preserve useful room-temperature mechanical performance.
The proposed protection is applicable in air at temperatures up to 1000 °C for exposures lasting hours to days.
The proposed protection is applicable under mechanical loading at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis asserts preservation of room-temperature mechanical performance, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that the effects of the addition on room-temperature mechanical performance are unknown.
